claims.text: Retrieval-augmented generation leverages information retrieval and generative models to handle real-time and domain-specific knowledge.
Limitations within retrieval-augmented generation components cause hallucinations in generated outputs.
Causes of hallucinations in retrieval-augmented large language models stem from sub-tasks in both the retrieval and generation phases.
Detection and correction methods reduce the impact of hallucinations in retrieval-augmented large language models.

evidence.description: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) leverages the strengths of information retrieval and generative models to enhance the handling of real-time and domain-specific knowledge.
limitations within RAG components may cause hallucinations, or more precisely termed confabulations in generated outputs
examine the causes of hallucinations from different sub-tasks in the retrieval and generation phases
investigate methods to reduce the impact of hallucination through detection and correction

methodologies.name: Literature Review and Categorization Framework
methodologies.description: A systematic review categorizing causes of hallucinations across retrieval and generation sub-tasks, along with mitigation, detection, and correction techniques.

limitations.text: Limitations within RAG components cause hallucinations or confabulations in generated outputs.

future_work.text: Future research directions for mitigating hallucinations in retrieval-augmented LLMs.
